title: feat: migrate to nested skilljar: YAML front matter (v0.2.0)
description:
## Summary

- Replaces the flat `skilljar_course_id` / `skilljar_lesson_id` / … front matter keys with a single nested `skilljar:` block, giving cleaner YAML and a single namespace for all Skilljar configuration
- Adds `parse_skilljar_fm()` internal helper with strict validation (aborts on flat keys, unknown keys, wrong types) and full unit-test coverage (16 tests)
- Updates `ci_write_lesson_id()` to patch the nested block surgically (text-based, no YAML round-trip); aborts when no `skilljar:` block present
- Bumps version to **0.2.0**

### Follow-up improvements (also in this PR)

- GHA detect block simplified to nested-only format; `lesson_order=0` falsy-Python bug fixed
- Workflow version header (`# quarjar-workflow-version: 0.2.0`) + runtime warn-only version check step
- Post-writeback YAML validation step guards against duplicate lesson creation
- README, `use_skilljar_workflow()` docs, and NEWS.md updated throughout

## Test Plan

- [ ] `devtools::test()` — 96 tests, 0 failures
- [ ] `devtools::check()` — 0 errors, 0 warnings
- [ ] Verify nested `skilljar:` front matter block is accepted end-to-end
- [ ] Verify flat `skilljar_*` keys produce an informative abort message
- [ ] Verify workflow version comment appears in installed workflow file

Feature/ci-helpers: simplify CI script by relying on package functions
description:
Add R/ci.R with five exported helpers that replace the verbose inline Rscript blocks in the GitHub Actions workflow:

- ci_generate_zip()            – render + timestamp ZIP, write GITHUB_OUTPUT
- ci_create_web_package()      – create pkg, poll until READY, capture old ID
- ci_create_or_update_lesson() – create/update routing, write GITHUB_OUTPUT
- ci_delete_old_web_package()  – non-fatal delete on the update path
- ci_write_lesson_id()         – inject skilljar_lesson_id into QMD front matter

The front-matter patching step now calls ci_write_lesson_id() via `Rscript -e`, removing the Python heredoc entirely. Each workflow step that previously contained 20–50 lines of inline R is now a two-liner. Logic is unchanged; the refactor is purely structural.

title: feat: update existing WEB_PACKAGE lessons on push
description:
- Add `update_lesson()` (PATCH /v1/lessons/{id}) to R/web_packages.R
- Workflow detects `skilljar_lesson_id` in .qmd front matter to choose create vs. update path; on first publish opens a PR to write the new
  lesson ID back into the front matter
- Remove workflow_dispatch trigger; all config lives in front matter
- Add `skilljar_lesson_order` and `skilljar_lesson_id` front matter fields
- Delete old web package after a successful lesson update
- Harden the PR-writeback step: idempotent push (--force-with-lease), idempotent PR creation (gh pr list guard), git diff guard to detect unchanged front matter, safe temp-file handling (trap + printf %s),
  and correct gh pr list error propagation
- Update CLAUDE.md and README.md to document the new workflow

add zip-publisher github action
description:
This makes it easier for users to adopt the workflow in their repositories.

Changes:
- Moved workflow from .github/workflows/ to inst/workflows/
  - Workflow isn't meant for this repo, only for users' repos
  - Allows package installation to include the workflow file

- Added use_skilljar_workflow() function
  - Copies workflow to user's .github/workflows/ directory
  - Checks for Git repository
  - Creates directory structure if needed
  - Prevents accidental overwrites (unless overwrite = TRUE)
  - Provides clear next-steps instructions
  - Links to full setup guide

- Updated documentation
  - GITHUB_ACTION_SETUP.md: Added use_skilljar_workflow() as Option A
  - README.md: Shows helper function as recommended approach
  - Both docs updated with new inst/workflows/ path

Usage:
```r
remotes::install_github("posit-dev/quarjar")
quarjar::use_skilljar_workflow()
```

This follows the pattern of usethis::use_github_action() and makes workflow adoption trivial for end users.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
